versions.notes:
Squads and revives, three new game modes, real sights, a soundtrack, and far fewer frame drops.

- Squads: you join a squad of four. Deploy on a squadmate; your squad is listed in a panel and marked in green.
- Defibrillator: a new Medic gadget. Stand over a fallen teammate and use it to bring them back where they fell.
- New game modes: Team Deathmatch (every death costs a ticket), Capture the Flag (first to three captures) and Rush (attackers arm two objectives a stage, three stages). Pick one in the match setup; servers set it in server.cfg (mode = tdm, ctf or rush).
- Sights are now real models: EOTech EXPS3, Aimpoint T-2 (an RMR on pistol slides), Trijicon RMR, Holosun HS510C, Vortex Spitfire 3x, ACOG TA31, Vortex Razor 1-6x, Leupold Mark 4 and Schmidt & Bender PM II. New: Aimpoint CompM4, and the PSO-1 4x on the AK side rail with its own rangefinder reticle.
- New attachments: the Grip-Pod (a vertical grip whose legs spread into a bipod) and an offset M300 light. Bipods stand when you go prone or rest the gun, for much less kick. The D-60 drum magazine is remodelled from photos.
- Lights and lasers switch on and off with L (others see them).
- Lean can be set to press instead of hold (Settings).
- The underbarrel grenade launchers now sit flush under the handguard.
- Performance: soldiers are now animated on the graphics card. The view at the deployment with 64 soldiers went from about 30 to over 150 fps on an RTX 5060 laptop, and the frequent drops are gone. A launch screen shows at once, and the title is up in under two seconds.
- New title screen with the version number on it.
- Colour: a new Colour setting (Natural, Rich, Vivid; Rich is the default) with deeper shadows and fuller colour, and smoother skies.
- Effects: sparks and embers in explosions, dust and sparks where bullets hit, muzzle sparks, embers above fires, dust from slides and dives, and dust in the air.
- Soundtrack: a title theme, a deploy piece, a battle theme at the start of a match, and victory and defeat themes. Music has its own volume slider.
- Fixed: bullets and rockets at neck height went through a soldier between the chest and the head.
- The web version has a Servers page too, and the official server now takes players from the browser as well as from Windows and Linux (join it from Servers).
- Servers must be 0.1.7 too. The official server runs 0.1.7.

The underbarrel launcher on servers, and finer soldiers, guns and attachments.

- Fixed: on a server (the official one included), B said there was no launcher under the gun even with an M203 or GP-25 fitted. A joining player's game misread the launcher's name and built a plain rifle in its place. B now brings the launcher up on servers as it does offline, and its grenades fly.
- Soldiers close to you (within about 16 m) are drawn in finer detail: rounder limbs, boots, hands and helmets, pocket snaps, knee pad ribs and buckles, boot tread and eyelets, a sleeve pocket with a flag patch, glove seams, the shirt's collar and zip, webbing loops round the vest and belt, buckles, zips, a drag handle, a helmet light, strobe and shock cord. Your own arms are always drawn this way. Soldiers further off keep the plain body, so a full 32-a-side fight costs about the same.
- Attachments: clamp nuts and bolts, adjuster screws, lens rings, ring screws on scopes, flutes and vents on suppressors, notched bipod legs, a light's bezel and tail switch, lenses, knobs and a selector on laser boxes, the drum's winding key.
- Every gun's round parts (barrels, tubes, grips, knobs) are smoother.
- The first match after updating takes longer to load (about 20 seconds) while the new parts are shaded; after that it's as quick as before.
- Servers must be 0.1.6 too. The official server runs 0.1.6.

Tighter maps, swimming, ammo types and controller button prompts.

- Every map is tighter: the play area is about a sixth smaller across, the deployments sit closer, and the open ground between them now has forward posts, huts, low walls, groves and loose cover.
- Swimming: deep water floats you with your eyes just above the surface. You swim slower than you walk (faster with sprint held), the gun stays lowered, and you walk out at a bank or press Jump at a quay to climb out. Bots keep out of deep water and cross by the bridges.
- Ammo types, a new slot in Create a class: standard, hollow point (harder up close, falls off sooner), armour piercing (goes through thin walls) and subsonic (slow, near silent under a suppressor) for rifles, SMGs and pistols; buckshot, slugs and flechettes for shotguns.
- Underbarrel launchers: B (d-pad left on a controller) switches to the M203 or GP-25 and back. With no launcher fitted it now says so, and a tag beside the ammo shows the launcher, its rounds and its button.
- Controller prompts: with a controller in hand, the HUD and loading tips show its buttons (LB and RB for gadgets, d-pad up for killstreaks, X to reload) instead of keys. Keyboard prompts show your own key bindings.
- Servers must be 0.1.5 too: the maps changed, so a 0.1.4 game and a 0.1.5 server build different worlds. The official server runs 0.1.5.
- Known: a rocket can now and then pass through a soldier who has only just spawned.

32 a side, a reworked M32 and typing on the Steam Deck.

- Every map is bigger, made for 32 a side: five flags across a wider front, with an outpost on each flank (a logging camp, a radio relay, a mud-house hamlet, checkpoints, a radar site, a hangar yard, a farmstead, bridges over Timberline's river, dockside depots at Port Anvil), and deployments further back behind an approach of cover, forward posts and tree lines.
- Bots go up to 32 a side (16 by default), tickets up to 1200. Dedicated servers run 32 a side by default, the official server too.
- M32: the frame swings open to the side, each grenade goes into the chamber beside the barrel and the cylinder winds round to the next one. Its red dot sight is no longer blocked.
- Steam Deck: the on-screen keyboard types into the game's text boxes (server address, sign-in) and opens by itself when you pick one. Enter joins from the address box.
- Servers must be 0.1.4 too: the maps changed, so a 0.1.3 game and a 0.1.4 server build different worlds.
- Known: with your whole side in view at the deployment the frame rate dips for the first seconds of a 32-a-side match; a rocket can now and then pass through a soldier who has only just spawned.

Accounts, a server list and an official server.

- Accounts: sign in or make one from the title screen (top right) or at https://129-80-83-173.sslip.io. Your account name is your name on every scoreboard; without one you play as Guest and a number.
- Servers: a new page on the title screen lists every running dedicated server with its map and players, and joins in one click. Dedicated servers list themselves; a hosted game can be listed from the match setup.
- Official server: Frontface official (US East) is up for signed-in players.
- The scoreboard fits a full server: rows shrink to fit, and past about 30 a side it scrolls with the mouse wheel.
- Aim over cover, launchers with real ballistics and bigger blasts, flush M203 and GP-25 underbarrel launchers with their own sight, a side-mounted Kobra, and reticles you choose per class.
- Bots move as squads and go for the flags first.
- Known issue: a bot crouched right behind a wall can poke its rifle muzzle through it.

Resolution fix.

- The Resolution list under Settings > Graphics uses the monitor's real size, the same one the full-screen fix snaps back to (Proton on the Steam Deck reported a wrong size).
- Everything from 0.1.1: the native Linux / Steam Deck build and the full-screen fix for Proton.

Frontface for the Steam Deck and Linux, and a full-screen fix.

- Native Linux / Steam Deck build: install it with the Frontface Launcher AppImage (no Proton needed). Windows and Deck players can join each other's servers.
- Full screen at the wrong shape (side bars under Proton) now snaps back to the monitor's size.
- Display (full screen or windowed) and Resolution settings under Settings > Graphics.
- Controller mapping for Linux.

First build through the launcher.

- Conquest on six maps against bots or other players, with your own classes.
- Guns from every class's list, launchers, gadgets and killstreaks.
- Controller support, steady aim, stims for every class.
- Join a server by address from the launcher, or host one from the title screen.
